dates: 3 May - 5 May (journey begins 1 May from Munich)
summary: Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travels east by train through Munich, Vienna, Buda-Pesth and Klausenburgh to Bistritz to meet his client Count Dracula. He notes local food, costumes and Transylvanian superstition after researching the country in the British Museum. At the Golden Krone Hotel in Bistritz he receives a welcome letter from the Count; the landlord and his wife grow frightened at the mention of the Count, and on the eve of St. George's Day the landlady begs him not to go and gives him a crucifix on a rosary. Peasants cross themselves, make the sign against the evil eye and press protective gifts on him as the diligence climbs through the Carpathians to the Borgo Pass. At the pass the Count's black-horsed calèche arrives early, driven by a tall, strong, red-eyed stranger. During the night drive near midnight dogs and wolves howl, blue flames flicker over the ground where the driver stops to pile stones, and a ring of wolves surrounds the carriage until the driver waves them away. The chapter ends as the calèche enters the courtyard of a vast ruined castle.

scenes.title: Rail journey to Klausenburgh
scenes.location: Train Munich - Vienna - Buda-Pesth - Klausenburgh; Hotel Royale
scenes.summary: Harker travels east, notes the Danube bridges and the feeling of leaving the West, and eats paprika hendl at the Hotel Royale.
scenes.key_quote: The impression I had was that we were leaving the West and entering the East

scenes.title: Night at Hotel Royale and morning train
scenes.time: night of 3 May to morning of 4 May
scenes.summary: A dog howls under his window all night; thirsty from paprika he drains the carafe. Breakfast of mamaliga and impletata; the late train dawdles through hill country with castles and flooded riverbeds; stations full of costumed peasants and Slovaks.
scenes.key_quote: There was a dog howling all night under my window

scenes.title: Arrival at Bistritz and the Golden Krone
scenes.summary: At twilight Harker reaches the old frontier town, is greeted by the landlady who hands over Dracula's letter announcing the diligence at three next day and a carriage at the Borgo Pass.
scenes.mood: quaint, expectant, first hint of strangeness
scenes.key_quote: Welcome to the Carpathians. I am anxiously expecting you.

scenes.title: The landlady's warning and the crucifix
scenes.summary: The couple cross themselves at the Count's name and refuse to speak. The landlady kneels, explains it is the eve of St. George's Day when evil has full sway at midnight, and forces her crucifix and rosary on him.
scenes.key_quote: Do you not know that to-night, when the clock strikes midnight, all the evil things in the world will have full sway?

scenes.title: The inn-yard crowd and the coach departs
scenes.location: Inn-yard of the Golden Krone, with oleander and orange trees in tubs
scenes.summary: Harker overhears words like Ordog, pokol, stregoica, vrolok and vlkoslak; the crowd crosses itself and points two fingers at him against the evil eye as the four-horse coach leaves.
scenes.key_quote: all made the sign of the cross and pointed two fingers towards me

scenes.title: Drive through the Mittel Land and into the Carpathians
scenes.location: Mittel Land road to Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: Orchards in bloom, pine woods like tongues of flame, snowy peaks, wayside crosses and shrines, hay-ricks in trees, leiter-wagons. The driver refuses to let Harker walk because of fierce dogs and rushes the horses.
scenes.key_quote: No, no, you must not walk here; the dogs are too fierce

scenes.title: Gifts of protection in the Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: As darkness falls the passengers urge the driver faster and press odd gifts on Harker with blessings. The pass opens under thundery clouds; there is no carriage waiting and the driver says to go on to Bukovina.
scenes.key_quote: It seemed as though the mountain range had separated two atmospheres

scenes.title: The Count's calèche arrives
scenes.summary: Horses scream and plunge as a calèche with four coal-black horses overtakes the coach. The tall bearded driver with red-glinting eyes, sharp white teeth and steel grip takes Harker's bags; a passenger murmurs the Lenore line about the dead travelling fast.

scenes.title: Circling drive and midnight howling
scenes.location: Roads of the Pass, in the calèche
scenes.summary: Cloak and rug, a flask of slivovitz under the seat. The carriage seems to double back over the same ground. At midnight dogs howl, then wolves; the driver soothes the panicked horses with whispers and then turns down a narrow road under arching trees as snow begins.
scenes.key_quote: it was within a few minutes of midnight

scenes.title: Blue flames and the ring of wolves
scenes.location: Narrow wooded road and rocky ground beside the Pass
scenes.summary: Faint blue flames appear; the driver stops, vanishes into the dark and arranges stones into a device (the flame does not flicker when he stands in front of it). Later wolves ring the carriage in silence; Harker shouts and beats the calèche; the driver stands in the road and sweeps his arms, and the wolves fall back and vanish.
scenes.key_quote: As he swept his long arms, as though brushing aside some impalpable obstacle, the wolves fell back and back further still.

scenes.title: Arrival at the ruined castle
scenes.summary: The carriage climbs steadily and halts in the courtyard of a vast ruined castle with tall black windows and broken battlements.
scenes.key_quote: a vast ruined castle, from whose tall black windows came no ray of light

locations.name: Golden Krone Hotel, Bistritz
locations.description: Thoroughly old-fashioned inn with a wide archway to an inn-yard; guests' room upstairs; bench outside the door where locals sit.
features: inn-yard with oleander and orange trees in green tubs
locations.atmosphere: quaint but fearful; staff cross themselves
locations.quote: thoroughly old-fashioned, for of course I wanted to see all I could of the ways of the country

locations.name: Bistritz
locations.description: Old frontier town near the Borgo Pass with a stormy history: five great fires fifty years earlier, and a three-week siege in the early seventeenth century that killed 13,000.
locations.quote: it has had a very stormy existence, and it certainly shows marks of it

locations.name: Hotel Royale, Klausenburgh
locations.description: Comfortable hotel where Harker sups on paprika hendl and breakfasts on mamaliga and impletata.
locations.atmosphere: warm but troubled by howling dog
locations.quote: I stopped for the night at the Hotel Royale

locations.name: Mittel Land road
locations.description: Rugged road through green swelling hills, orchards in blossom, steep hills crowned with farmhouses with blank gable ends, pine woods running down like tongues of flame.
locations.atmosphere: idyllic then threatening as dusk falls
locations.quote: a bewildering mass of fruit blossom—apple, plum, pear, cherry

locations.name: Carpathian mountains vista
locations.description: Mighty forested slopes, blue and purple shadowed peaks, jagged crags, snowy summits glowing pink at sunset, waterfalls glimpsed in rifts; the peak called Isten szek, God's seat.
locations.quote: the snowy mountain-top still held the sunset, and seemed to glow out with a delicate cool pink

locations.name: Borgo Pass
locations.description: Cleft in the hills where mountains frown down on both sides; sandy white road; the eastern side opens under rolling thundercloud.
locations.quote: the mountains seemed to come nearer to us on each side and to frown down upon us

locations.name: Wooded side road and stone-pile glade
locations.description: Narrow road turning sharply right, trees arching into a tunnel, frowning rocks, powdery snow; blue flame spots where the driver stacks stones.
locations.quote: Soon we were hemmed in with trees, which in places arched right over the roadway till we passed as through a tunnel

locations.name: Castle Dracula courtyard (arrival)
locations.description: Courtyard of a vast ruined castle with tall black windows and broken jagged battlements against the moonlit sky.
locations.quote: whose broken battlements showed a jagged line against the moonlit sky

characters.name: Jonathan Harker
characters.clothing: travelling clothes; later a cloak and rug from the driver
characters.personality: practical, curious, note-taking, mildly sceptical, loyal to Mina and his employer; keeps memos on recipes to get for Mina
characters.speech_style: polite, plain English; smattering of German
notable_lines: My duty was imperative, and that I must go.

characters.name: Count Dracula (as unnamed driver)
characters.role: driver of the calèche, secretly the Count
characters.appearance: tall man, long brown beard, great black hat hiding the face, very bright eyes that seem red in lamplight, hard mouth, very red lips, sharp ivory-white teeth, grip of steel
notable_lines: You are early to-night, my friend.
You cannot deceive me, my friend; I know too much, and my horses are swift.
abilities: commands wolves with a sweep of the arm
sees blue flames and marks them with stones

characters.name: The landlady of the Golden Krone
characters.clothing: white undergarment with long double apron front and back of coloured stuff
characters.speech_style: mixes German with another language when hysterical
notable_lines: Must you go? Oh! young Herr, must you go?

characters.name: The landlord
characters.personality: reticent, pretends not to understand German

characters.name: The coach driver (diligence)
characters.appearance: wide linen drawers covering the box-seat ('gotza')
characters.personality: grimly humorous, nervous of the night
notable_lines: No, no, you must not walk here; the dogs are too fierce
There is no carriage here. The Herr is not expected after all.

characters.name: Slovaks
characters.appearance: long black hair, heavy black moustaches
characters.clothing: big cow-boy hats, baggy dirty-white trousers, white linen shirts, leather belts nearly a foot wide studded with brass nails, high boots

objects.name: Crucifix on rosary
objects.description: Crucifix taken from the landlady's neck and hung on Harker's neck on a rosary.
objects.function_in_story: Gift of protection; comfort to Harker.
objects.quote: she put the rosary round my neck, and said, “For your mother’s sake,”

objects.name: Dracula's letter of welcome
objects.description: Letter left at the Golden Krone, signed 'Dracula', announcing the diligence at three and the carriage at the Borgo Pass.
objects.location_or_owner: Held by the landlord for Harker
objects.quote: At the Borgo Pass my carriage will await you and will bring you to me.

objects.name: Polyglot dictionary
objects.description: Dictionary in Harker's bag used to translate overheard words.
objects.function_in_story: Reveals Ordog, pokol, stregoica, vrolok, vlkoslak.
objects.quote: I quietly got my polyglot dictionary from my bag

objects.name: Protective gifts from passengers (garlic, wild rose, mountain ash named in ch. 3)
objects.description: Odd and varied gifts pressed on Harker at the Borgo Pass with blessings; chapter 3 identifies garlic, wild rose and mountain ash.
objects.quote: several of the passengers offered me gifts, which they pressed upon me with an earnestness which would take no denial

objects.name: Flask of slivovitz
objects.description: Plum brandy of the country under the calèche's seat.
objects.location_or_owner: Underneath the seat of the calèche
objects.quote: There is a flask of slivovitz (the plum brandy of the country) underneath the seat

objects.name: Cloak and rug
objects.description: Thrown over Harker's shoulders and knees in the calèche.
objects.quote: a cloak was thrown over my shoulders, and a rug across my knees

objects.name: Calèche
objects.description: Light carriage drawn by four coal-black horses.
objects.quote: a calèche, with four horses, drove up behind us

objects.name: Diligence / coach
objects.description: Crazy coach on great leather springs, four small horses abreast, lamps.
objects.function_in_story: Carries Harker to the Borgo Pass.
objects.quote: the crazy coach rocked on its great leather springs

objects.name: Leiter-wagon
objects.description: Ordinary peasant cart with a long, snake-like vertebra frame.
objects.function_in_story: Local colour; later used by Slovaks.
objects.quote: with its long, snake-like vertebra, calculated to suit the inequalities of the road

objects.name: Driver's whip
objects.quote: cracked his big whip over his four small horses

objects.name: Paprika hendl, robber steak, mamaliga, impletata
objects.description: Chicken with red pepper; bacon, onion and beef on sticks roasted over fire; maize-flour porridge; stuffed egg-plant with forcemeat.
objects.quote: “robber steak”—bits of bacon, onion, and beef, seasoned with red pepper, and strung on sticks

objects.name: Golden Mediasch wine
objects.description: Local wine with a queer sting on the tongue.

objects.name: Stone device at the blue flame
objects.description: Small stones gathered by the driver and formed into some device on the spot of each flame.
objects.quote: gathering a few stones, formed them into some device

objects.name: Match and pocket watch
objects.description: Harker strikes a match to check his watch (nearly midnight).
objects.quote: I struck a match, and by its flame looked at my watch

objects.name: Carriage lamps
objects.description: Lamps lit by the driver; flickering light.
objects.quote: The only stop he would make was a moment’s pause to light his lamps.

objects.name: Roadside crosses and shrines
objects.description: Crosses by the road and shrines before which peasants kneel.
objects.quote: By the roadside were many crosses

objects.name: Harker's luggage
objects.description: Bags handed to the calèche driver.
objects.quote: my bags were handed out and put in the calèche

creatures.name: Wolves
creatures.description: Long, sinewy limbs, shaggy hair, white teeth and lolling red tongues; form a silent ring around the calèche.
creatures.behaviour: Howl in answer to the dogs at midnight; encircle prey in silence; obey the driver's arm sweeps.
creatures.quote: a ring of wolves, with white teeth and lolling red tongues, with long, sinewy limbs and shaggy hair

creatures.name: Village dogs
creatures.description: Farm dogs that howl at midnight.
creatures.behaviour: Take up one another's howls; fierce on the hills.
creatures.quote: a long, agonised wailing, as if from fear

creatures.name: Coal-black horses
creatures.description: Splendid coal-black team of four drawing the calèche.
creatures.behaviour: Rear and sweat with fear at wolves but are calmed by the driver's whispering.
creatures.quote: the horses were coal-black and splendid animals

creatures.name: Dracula (disguised as coachman)
creatures.description: Seemingly human driver with superhuman strength, red-gleaming eyes and sharp teeth.
creatures.behaviour: Controls animals, vanishes, appears at the right time.
creatures.quote: his strength must have been prodigious

creatures.name: Blue flames
creatures.description: Faint flickering blue flame over the ground that casts no light on its surroundings and does not obstruct when a person passes in front.
creatures.behaviour: Appear in the night; the driver marks each with stones.
creatures.quote: Suddenly, away on our left, I saw a faint flickering blue flame.

vampire_lore.rule: Eve of St. George's Day: evil things have full sway at midnight
vampire_lore.detail: Local belief reported by the landlady; the night of 4-5 May.
vampire_lore.quote: all the evil things in the world will have full sway

vampire_lore.rule: The evil-eye guard: cross and two pointed fingers
vampire_lore.detail: Crowd makes the sign of the cross and points two fingers at Harker as a charm against the evil eye.
vampire_lore.quote: a charm or guard against the evil eye

vampire_lore.rule: Crucifix and protective plants given as wards
vampire_lore.detail: Crucifix, rosary, and (named later) garlic, wild rose, mountain ash.
vampire_lore.quote: each was given in simple good faith, with a kindly word, and a blessing

vampire_lore.detail: Ordog (Satan), pokol (hell), stregoica (witch), vrolok (Slovak) and vlkoslak (Servian) meaning were-wolf or vampire.
vampire_lore.quote: “vrolok” and “vlkoslak”—both of which mean the same thing

vampire_lore.detail: Wolves fall back at his arm-sweep; horses calm at his whisper.
vampire_lore.quote: the wolves fell back and back further still

vampire_lore.detail: Grip of steel, lifts and handles luggage easily.
vampire_lore.quote: a hand which caught my arm in a grip of steel

vampire_lore.rule: Blue flame marks hidden treasure on this night
vampire_lore.detail: Folk belief explained in chapter 2; the driver follows the flames.

vampire_lore.rule: Eyes glow red; very red lips and sharp white teeth
vampire_lore.quote: a pair of very bright eyes, which seemed red in the lamplight

vampire_lore.detail: Line from Burger's Lenore whispered by a passenger who recognises the driver.
When the driver stood between Harker and the flame he did not obstruct it; he seems insubstantial to light.
vampire_lore.quote: when he stood between me and the flame he did not obstruct it

puzzles.name: The circling carriage
puzzles.setup: The calèche seems to loop back on the same road near midnight.
puzzles.obstacle: Harker is disoriented and unable to ask the driver.
puzzles.book_solution: He takes note of a salient point and confirms they are going in circles; the driver is stalling until midnight.
puzzles.game_idea: Memorise landmarks on a looping route to detect the stall; choose to speak up or stay silent.
puzzles.quote: I took note of some salient point, and found that this was so.

puzzles.name: Reading the village words
puzzles.setup: The crowd repeats strange words around Harker.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker looks them up in his polyglot dictionary.
puzzles.game_idea: Collect overheard words and match them in a dictionary UI to unlock lore entries.
puzzles.quote: I quietly got my polyglot dictionary from my bag and looked them out.

puzzles.name: Reading the road for the missing carriage
puzzles.setup: No carriage at the pass an hour before the stated time.
puzzles.obstacle: Driver wants to carry Harker on to Bukovina.
puzzles.book_solution: Dracula arrives and overrides the driver.
puzzles.game_idea: Timing puzzle: be at the pass at the right moment, choose to board the coach or wait.

combat.name: Wolf ring in the pass
weapons_used: Harker shouts and beats the calèche side
combat.tactics: Harker is helpless; wolves encircle silently while the driver is away; noise tries to open a gap; the driver ends it by command.
combat.game_idea: Defensive survival encounter: protect the horses for 3 rounds by making noise/light; panic meter on horses; the ring breaks only when a scripted event triggers.
combat.quote: but the living ring of terror encompassed them on every side

dialogue_samples.speaker: Dracula (driver)
dialogue_samples.line: The night is chill, mein Herr, and my master the Count bade me take all care of you.

quest_hooks: Decide whether to accept or refuse the landlady's crucifix (and keep it for later wards).
Collect the protective gifts offered by passengers (garlic, wild rose, mountain ash).
Survive the night drive: watch the clock, count the loops, endure the wolf ring.
Learn the local words for vampire and unlock lore.
Choose whether to leave the coach at the Borgo Pass.
